texts.61:
England, the Animals, as a warm-up act (they weren’t televised but were so good that Hamp edited their performance into a video release of the show later) and by the time Vincent was finished with his rousing set the crowd was positively foaming. Battling jet-lag and calling on his storehouse of native energy, Jerry Lee strutted into the studio wearing a black suit, white shirt, dark tie, and pointy-toed white-leather shoes, and gave himself over to Hamp and Casson’s masterstroke vision for his entrance: he would descend from the heavens unto the eager crowd courtesy of a hydraulic platform, on which a Challen grand piano, bench, and Fender amp had been ceremoniously and, Jerry Lee trusted, sturdily placed. The crowd erupted when he hit the first chords of “Great Balls Of Fire,” Jerry Lee sounding as if he characteristically expected his backing band — on this occasion the Flintstones — to know when he was going to kick it off, but they had to catch up from the start. Surveying his British kingdom, Jerry Lee grinningly works his way through the tune, held aloft a dozen feet in the air while the Flintstones bash away gleefully beneath him. His right leg pounding 4/4, he whoops it up while couples clap and dance and twist and gape open-mouthed up at him. Casson’s four-camera, multi-angle direction reflected the era’s excitement with rock & roll’s new rhythmic, sexuallyplayful, urban power. The cameras (“these big chunky things,” Casson chuckles) moved with some difficulty among the dancing crowd, Casson nonetheless committed to capturing the reckless vibe of the floor. Rotary-lens shots move among aerial views of the dancing crowd and hip set design, medium shots of Jerry Lee at the piano, and close-ups of his already-perspiring (and, it must be said, somewhat puffy) face, where the cameras capture a

telling mix of concentration, bemusement, and mild surprise. I mean I know I’m this good and I know that I deserve it but really now . . . **Boy Pablo** (stylized as **boy pablo**) (born 29 November 1998) is the indie pop music project of Norwegian singer songwriter **Nicolas Muñoz**. Muñoz writes, records, performs, and produces all of the project's music. The project has been inactive since 2022. Boy Pablo's latest touring lineup consisted of Nicolás Muñoz (guitar, vocals), Gabriel Muñoz (lead guitar), Judah Kubendran (bass guitar) and Esteban Muñoz (drums).
Boy Pablo gained attention in late 2017 after the music video for the song "Everytime" gained international popularity on YouTube.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:2-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-bgtwo2-3) The duology concept EPs _Roy Pablo_ (2017) and _Soy Pablo_ (2018) were released under Boy Pablo's own independent label 777 Music. His debut studio album, _Wachito Rico_ was released in October 2020. Out of nominations for five Spellemann Awards, Boy Pablo has won one, and has additionally been nominated for three _GAFFA_ Awards and one P3 Gull award, having won the latter.

Nicolás Pablo Rivera Muñoz[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-4) (born 29 November 1998)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-6) was born and raised in Bergen after his Chilean parents immigrated to Norway in the 1980s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-8) Born into a musical family as the youngest child, his father and brother were both multi-instrumentalists and helped teach him how to play guitar, drums, bass guitar and piano.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-9) He attended secondary school at Kongshaug Upper Secondary School of Music, a music boarding school in nearby Os.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:3-11) He and his parents moved to Os Municipality when he started secondary school, two years prior to January 2017.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:OsMove-12)

### 2015–2016: Career beginnings
[edit]
Muñoz began the "Boy Pablo" project in December 2015, and released his debut single "Flowers" in January 2016.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:3-11) He played his first-ever gig as a warm-up band for Tellef Raabe (brother of Norwegian singer Sigrid) at Hulen in April 2016.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:3-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-13) In September 2016, he performed as part of the Vill Vill Vest festival in Bergen.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-14) Boy Pablo gained immense national popularity after receiving a Bergenfest scholarship of 35 thousand kroner in November 2016. Alongside this scholarship, he additionally won his own headlining gig as well as a performance at the 2017 Bergenfest.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-15)

### 2017–2019: _Roy Pablo_ and _Soy Pablo_
[edit]
Muñoz further gained international popularity in 2017 with the song and music video for "Everytime", originally uploaded to YouTube in May 2017. Within a few weeks, the video had received millions of views, with Muñoz significantly expanding his fanbase.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:2-1) Boy Pablo released the 6-song EP, _Roy Pablo_, in May 2017, which includes "Everytime". In August 2017, Boy Pablo opened as a supporting act for American band Beach Fossils at Red Bull Sound Select in Oslo.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-16)
Boy Pablo released the single "Losing You" in March 2018,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-pitchfork1-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-pigeon22-18) and embarked on a sold out thirty-nine date headlining world tour of United States, Europe and Asia.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-19) On 5 October 2018 Boy Pablo released his second EP, _Soy Pablo_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-20) The EP received critical acclaim and was successful commercially in Norway, topping the national Vinyl albums chart.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:1-21) The EP additionally landed in the top 10 of year-end critics lists from Gaffa and Nöjesguiden, placing at Nos.

### 2017–2019: _Roy Pablo_ and _Soy Pablo_
9 and 4 respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-23) At the 2018 Spellemannprisen (also referred to as Norwegian Grammy Awards), Boy Pablo was awarded with the award for Breakthrough of the Year which additionally gave him the Gramo scholarship of 250.000 kroner.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-25) At the same ceremony he was nominated in the categories of Best International Success,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-26) and Indie/Alternative of the Year for _Soy Pablo_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-27) At the 2018 P3 Gull Awards, Boy Pablo also won Årets Nykommer.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:4-28) In January 2019, Boy Pablo was the only Norwegian artist to perform at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in California, U.S. in that year.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-30) At the 2019 Spellemannprisen (also referred to as Norwegian Grammy Awards), Boy Pablo was nominated for Best International Success for the second consecutive year in addition to Årets Musikkvideo ("Losing You").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-31)

### 2017–2019: _Roy Pablo_ and _Soy Pablo_
In May 2020, Boy Pablo announced the release of his debut studio album, _Wachito Rico_;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-32) the title is a Chilean expression and means "handsome boy."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-33) The album's singles are "Hey Girl", "Honey" and "Rest Up". With the release of the latter single, Boy Pablo announced his second-ever headlining world tour to support _Wachito Rico_, which kicked off in the UK in March 2021.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-34)
In the second half of 2022, after completing a tour in Latin America and shortly after releasing his latest single, "Be Mine", Boy Pablo announced the cancelation of his upcoming tours in North America and Asia,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-35) citing health problems and lack of energy. Boy Pablo has remained inactive in music since then.

Muñoz cites Mac DeMarco, Veronica Maggio, Tyler, the Creator, the Beatles, Arctic Monkeys, Tame Impala and Mild High Club as musical influences.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-p3one-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-brescia2-38) His rise to fame with a DIY-produced bedroom pop track,"Everytime" (2017), which gained popularity through the YouTube algorithm has drawn comparisons to that of American singer Clairo's rise to fame with her video for "Pretty Girl" (2017).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-nattogdag12-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-40)

**Isimeme** "**Naomi**" **Udu** (born November 16, 1998), known professionally as **Hemlocke Springs** (stylized in all lowercase), is an American singer, songwriter, and record producer. She first gained prominence for her second self-produced song "Girlfriend" achieving viral popularity on video-sharing platform TikTok. The majority of her discography is characterized by 1980ssynth-pop and 2000s pop sounds.
During her postgraduate medical studies at Dartmouth College in 2021, Udu began to upload unnamed songs on SoundCloud, only to quickly remove them. Hemlocke Springs's first official single "Gimme All Ur Luv" (categorized as bedroom pop) was subsequently self-released in 2022. She later released her debut extended play, _Going...Going...Gone!_, in 2023. Her debut album, _The Apple Tree Under the Sea_, was released on February 13, 2026.

## Early life and education
[edit]
Isimeme Udu was born to two Nigerian immigrant parents on November 16, 1998, in Raleigh, North Carolina.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-1) Nicknamed as "Naomi" from her parents, she grew up in Concord alongside her brother, a musician and SoundCloud producer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-2) In her sophomore year of high school, Udu took a choir course and met a freshman classmate, MJ, who taught her to create music using GarageBand.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Gunn-3)
Udu graduated from Spelman College with a bachelor's degree in biology in 2021. Two years later, she graduated with a master's degree in medical informatics from Dartmouth College.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-4)

## Early life and education
### 2021–2023: Career beginnings with "Girlfriend"
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hemlocke_Springs&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2021–2023: Career beginnings with \"Girlfriend\"")]
While studying at Dartmouth College in 2021, Udu began to release various unnamed songs on SoundCloud, only to quickly remove them. The next year, she decided to shed her embarrassment and uploaded a demo titled "Jacob" under the name Hemlocke Springs.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Spanos-5) Afterwards, she independently released her self-produced song "Gimme All Ur Luv" on May 24, 2022. It gained over a million streams through Swedish streaming service Spotify and was considered one of "the best bedroom pop [songs]" by entertainment company Complex Networks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-6) In an interview with magazine _Rolling Stone_, she said the song was written during a period of depression at school; she considered deleting it but changed her mind when she saw Canadian musician Grimes had commented.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Spanos-5)
As she worked at the library at her university, Hemlocke Springs shared snippets of her second song on video-sharing platform TikTok, which achieved viral popularity.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Slocum-7) Shortly afterward, "Girlfriend" was released on November 2_[citation needed_]. The song was positively received by critics and audiences, deemed an "awkward Black girl anthem"_[citation needed_] and surpassing a million streams on Spotify. In an interview with _People_, Udu stated that she felt honored by the song's success, but was confused by her sudden rise to fame.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-8)

## Early life and education
### 2021–2023: Career beginnings with "Girlfriend"
_New Musical Express_ later named her as one of the "essential emerging artists" for recognizing her "bright and breezy bangers" on January 6, 2023.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-:Flood-9) The same month, Hemlocke Springs released her third song, "Stranger Danger!", a critique of capitalism.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-10) During May to August 2023, she began working with English record producer Burns and released three more songs.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-11) Her first festival performance occurred on July 21 at the Adult Swim Festival for the annual entertainment event San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-12) "Enknee1" was released a month later with the artist announcing her debut extended play (EP) named _Going...Going...Gone!_, released on September 29, 2023.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-13) A month later, _Pitchfork_ praised and described Hemlocke Springs' music aesthetics as "kitschy and yearning", where every song of the EP "can be imagined in a different scene" from a 1980s romantic comedy film.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-14)

## Early life and education
### 2021–2023: Career beginnings with "Girlfriend"
Hemlocke Springs began touring across North America and Europe[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-15) and was invited to be an opening act for American band Muna's [Life's So Fun Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life's_So_Fun_Tour "Life's So Fun Tour") and rapper Ashnikko's Weedkiller Tour.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Slocum-7) She was later featured in a magazine double issue with other notable artists, published through _DIY_ on December 11, 2023.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-16)

**Boy Pablo** (stylized as **boy pablo**) (born 29 November 1998) is the indie pop music project of Norwegian singer songwriter **Nicolas Muñoz**. Muñoz writes, records, performs, and produces all of the project's music. The project has been inactive since 2022. Boy Pablo's latest touring lineup consisted of Nicolás Muñoz (guitar, vocals), Gabriel Muñoz (lead guitar), Judah Kubendran (bass guitar) and Esteban Muñoz (drums).
Boy Pablo gained attention in late 2017 after the music video for the song "Everytime" gained international popularity on YouTube.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-:2-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Pablo#cite_note-bgtwo2-3) The duology concept EPs _Roy Pablo_ (2017) and _Soy Pablo_ (2018) were released under Boy Pablo's own independent label 777 Music. His debut studio album, _Wachito Rico_ was released in October 2020. Out of nominations for five Spellemann Awards, Boy Pablo has won one, and has additionally been nominated for three _GAFFA_ Awards and one P3 Gull award, having won the latter.

**Isimeme** "**Naomi**" **Udu** (born November 16, 1998), known professionally as **Hemlocke Springs** (stylized in all lowercase), is an American singer, songwriter, and record producer. She first gained prominence for her second self-produced song "Girlfriend" achieving viral popularity on video-sharing platform TikTok. The majority of her discography is characterized by 1980ssynth-pop and 2000s pop sounds.
During her postgraduate medical studies at Dartmouth College in 2021, Udu began to upload unnamed songs on SoundCloud, only to quickly remove them. Hemlocke Springs's first official single "Gimme All Ur Luv" (categorized as bedroom pop) was subsequently self-released in 2022. She later released her debut extended play, _Going...Going...Gone!_, in 2023. Her debut album, _The Apple Tree Under the Sea_, was released on February 13, 2026.

## Early life and education

Isimeme Udu was born to two Nigerian immigrant parents on November 16, 1998, in Raleigh, North Carolina.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-1) Nicknamed as "Naomi" from her parents, she grew up in Concord alongside her brother, a musician and SoundCloud producer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-2) In her sophomore year of high school, Udu took a choir course and met a freshman classmate, MJ, who taught her to create music using GarageBand.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Gunn-3)
Udu graduated from Spelman College with a bachelor's degree in biology in 2021. Two years later, she graduated with a master's degree in medical informatics from Dartmouth College.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-4)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hemlocke_Springs&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2021–2023: Career beginnings with \"Girlfriend\"")]
While studying at Dartmouth College in 2021, Udu began to release various unnamed songs on SoundCloud, only to quickly remove them. The next year, she decided to shed her embarrassment and uploaded a demo titled "Jacob" under the name Hemlocke Springs.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Spanos-5) Afterwards, she independently released her self-produced song "Gimme All Ur Luv" on May 24, 2022. It gained over a million streams through Swedish streaming service Spotify and was considered one of "the best bedroom pop [songs]" by entertainment company Complex Networks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-6) In an interview with magazine _Rolling Stone_, she said the song was written during a period of depression at school; she considered deleting it but changed her mind when she saw Canadian musician Grimes had commented.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Spanos-5)
As she worked at the library at her university, Hemlocke Springs shared snippets of her second song on video-sharing platform TikTok, which achieved viral popularity.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-Slocum-7) Shortly afterward, "Girlfriend" was released on November 2_[citation needed_]. The song was positively received by critics and audiences, deemed an "awkward Black girl anthem"_[citation needed_] and surpassing a million streams on Spotify. In an interview with _People_, Udu stated that she felt honored by the song's success, but was confused by her sudden rise to fame.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemlocke_Springs#cite_note-8)

Great review of "Tales From The South" by BLACK MOUNTAIN PROPHET:
If there is one word that describes the music on this album that word would be authenticity. Everything about this album is authentic; the music, the playing and the production values. The music on this album is nothing less than a tour de force through the rich and rugged landscape that is American rock, country and blues and everything that falls in between these. Black Mountain Prophet is well read and versed in the various genres that has made American music over the past decades, even stretching back a century and on this album they dig deep into the legacy of some of the greatest American musicians we owe the music we listen to today.

# GROOVEYARD RECORDS | Great review of "Tales From The South" by BLACK MOUNTAIN PROPHET: | Facebook
The album opens up with two songs written in the swamplands once ruled by ZZ Top, heavy and thumping riffage driven by Jarrod England’s grovelling vocals, before mellowing down in "Whiskey Don’t Make Me Cry". This beautiful song meant many things when I first heard it; good song in its own right reminiscent of 1970s folk and country-tinted mainstream rock, with Doobie Bros. style vocal harmonies. Further in, and imagining the song being performed acoustic, it comes across as out of the songbook of the uniquely talented combo that was Poco. "Milk Skin Woman" is a hard & heavy hitting boogie rocker followed by "Bad Women" which sees the band swing as hard as it rocks, paying homage to the great funkadelic artists of the 1970s. And that’s how it goes, song by song, the heritage of the best of American music is echoed on this album in wonderfully crafted songs that are just as original and authentic as the music of the great artists that once ruled and have tutored the four members of the band and inspired their music. Still another favourite of mine on this album is its closing composition, "Mercy", a Jimmy Reed/Eddie Taylor style blues rocker, rough and unpolished as intended by the great bluesmen of old.
The music on this album is played live, straight onto the tape, nothing is overproduced, overprocessed, overarranged and there are no overdubs. On this album you hear the band, four musicians, give all they’ve got, warts’n’all. The music is loud and into your face as if you are standing next to a stamp-sized stage in some small town bar, totally authentic and unapologetic. Not many musicians would have the courage (or the ability) to do it this way, release an album made like this one. This band does not seek shelter and security in recording technologies but play you their music rejecting the support and safety of any such medium. That is perhaps what makes this great music so special; it’s played as it is meant to be heard. You can’t possibly ask more of any band. And that is what Black Mountain Prophet gives you.

Great review of "Tales From The South" by BLACK MOUNTAIN PROPHET:
If there is one word that describes the music on this album that word would be authenticity. Everything about this album is authentic; the music, the playing and the production values. The music on this album is nothing less than a tour de force through the rich and rugged landscape that is American rock, country and blues and everything that falls in between these. Black Mountain Prophet is well read and versed in the various genres that has made American music over the past decades, even stretching back a century and on this album they dig deep into the legacy of some of the greatest American musicians we owe the music we listen to today.

# GROOVEYARD RECORDS | Great review of "Tales From The South" by BLACK MOUNTAIN PROPHET: | Facebook
The album opens up with two songs written in the swamplands once ruled by ZZ Top, heavy and thumping riffage driven by Jarrod England’s grovelling vocals, before mellowing down in "Whiskey Don’t Make Me Cry". This beautiful song meant many things when I first heard it; good song in its own right reminiscent of 1970s folk and country-tinted mainstream rock, with Doobie Bros. style vocal harmonies. Further in, and imagining the song being performed acoustic, it comes across as out of the songbook of the uniquely talented combo that was Poco. "Milk Skin Woman" is a hard & heavy hitting boogie rocker followed by "Bad Women" which sees the band swing as hard as it rocks, paying homage to the great funkadelic artists of the 1970s. And that’s how it goes, song by song, the heritage of the best of American music is echoed on this album in wonderfully crafted songs that are just as original and authentic as the music of the great artists that once ruled and have tutored the four members of the band and inspired their music. Still another favourite of mine on this album is its closing composition, "Mercy", a Jimmy Reed/Eddie Taylor style blues rocker, rough and unpolished as intended by the great bluesmen of old.
The music on this album is played live, straight onto the tape, nothing is overproduced, overprocessed, overarranged and there are no overdubs. On this album you hear the band, four musicians, give all they’ve got, warts’n’all. The music is loud and into your face as if you are standing next to a stamp-sized stage in some small town bar, totally authentic and unapologetic. Not many musicians would have the courage (or the ability) to do it this way, release an album made like this one. This band does not seek shelter and security in recording technologies but play you their music rejecting the support and safety of any such medium. That is perhaps what makes this great music so special; it’s played as it is meant to be heard. You can’t possibly ask more of any band. And that is what Black Mountain Prophet gives you.

**Conan Lee Gray** (born December 5, 1998) is an American singer, songwriter and former YouTuber. He was born in Lemon Grove, California, and raised in Georgetown, Texas, where he began uploading vlogs, covers, and original songs to YouTube as a teenager. In 2018, Gray signed a record deal with Republic Records, which released his debut EP, _Sunset Season_ (2018).
Bolstered by the commercially successful songs "Maniac" and "Heather", his studio album _Kid Krow_ (2020), entered the U.S. _Billboard_ 200 at number five, making it the biggest U.S. artist debut of that year. His second studio album, _Superache_ (2022), debuted in the top ten in the chart, also doing so in the United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland, and the Netherlands. His third and fourth albums, _Found Heaven_ (2024) and _Wishbone_ (2025), peaked at numbers 14 and three on the _Billboard_ 200, respectively.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-1)

## Early life
Gray was born on December 5, 1998, in Lemon Grove, California, a suburb of San Diego.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Notion-4) His father is Irish and his mother is Japanese.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-5) As an infant, he moved with his family to Hiroshima, Japan, because his grandfather needed medical care after being diagnosed with cancer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Mier-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Cardenas-7) After his grandfather's death, the family moved back to California.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Lauren-8)
Gray's parents divorced when he was three years old and he was thereafter raised by a single mother.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Greenwood-9) In a "Draw My Life" video, he details his experiences with divorce as a young child.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:4-10) As his father was in the military, Gray moved nine times during his childhood, including two times during sixth grade. He was frequently bullied in grade school for being quiet.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-11)
Gray eventually settled as a preteen in Georgetown, Texas, where he remained for the rest of his teenage years. His life in central Texas inspired much of his art and music. He was accepted to UCLA, and moved to Los Angeles, California, in September 2017. However, he dropped out three months later to begin touring after he was signed to Republic Records.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-12)

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
Gray created his official YouTube channel in 2013,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Metro-13) and began making videos at age 15. His early videos were about topics such as baking and mainly focused on his everyday life.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:1-14) His vlog content centered heavily on his life in small-town Texas. He is often hailed for his appreciation of Americana-related nostalgia.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Paper-15) Gray has recorded music, showed his art, and created other videos for his vlog with more than 25 million views.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Greenwood-9)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:1-14)

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
Gray self-released his debut single, "Idle Town", in March 2017. The song gained over 14 million streams on Spotify and 12 million views on YouTube.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Paper-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-ido-16) He self-released his second single, "Grow", on September 1, 2017.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-18)_[non-primary source needed_] In October 2018, he released the single "Generation Why" on Republic Records,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-ido-16) which was called "a rallying call to millennials".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-19) In November 2018, he released the five-track EP _Sunset Season_, which includes the songs "Idle Town", "Generation Why", "Crush Culture", "Greek God", and "Lookalike". The EP peaked at No. 2 on the _Billboard_ Heatseekers Albums chart. Gray embarked on the Sunset Shows tour in support of the EP.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-20) Sometime in 2018, he trademarked GirlyBoy, Inc., his way of owning his masters. He used it for his fourth album, _Wishbone_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-21)
Gray in 2019

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
Gray made his late-night television debut on _Late Night with Seth Meyers_ on the eve of February 2019,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-23) before performing several shows as an opening act on Panic! at the Disco's Pray for the Wicked Tour.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Stan-24) He played concert festivals such as The Great Escape in addition to touring nationally.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-25) In February 2019, Gray re-released the single "The Other Side"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-The_Other_Side_Affinity-26) after originally publishing it on YouTube in 2016 on the eve of the first day of his senior year of high school.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-The_Other_Side_Affinity-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-The_Other_Side_MV-27) Between March and October 2019, he released three singles from his debut album, _Kid Krow_, "Checkmate", "Comfort Crowd", and "Maniac",[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-28) and an independent single, "The King".

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
In October 2019, Gray embarked on the Comfort Crowd Tour, his second headlining tour of North America, with support from acclaimed New Zealand musician Benee as well as American recording artist UMI.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-29) As of October 2019, Gray's catalog had gained over 250 million streams across all platforms collectively.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-30) He received the 2019 Shorty Award for Best YouTube Musician,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Shorty_Awards-31) and was nominated for Breakthrough Artist at the 2019 Streamy Awards.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:3-32)

## Career
### 2020–2021: _Kid Krow_
Throughout the second week of 2020, Gray shared daily hints about the title of his debut album on Twitter._[citation needed_] On January 9, 2020, he revealed the title, _Kid Krow_, and wrote, "I say more on this album than I've ever said in my life, and I can't wait to tell you all of my secrets.

Love y'all."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:5-33) Gray released "The Story" on the same day of the album's announcement,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-34) as well as "Wish You Were Sober" as a surprise release two days before the album's release.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-35) During early 2020, Gray's single "Maniac" became successful on international mainstream pop radio,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:7-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-40) specifically in Australia,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-42) where it was certified platinum.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-ARIA2020singles-43) The song was also certified Platinum in Canada and Gold in the US, making it his first certified song in all three countries.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:0-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-RIAA-45) It became his first appearance on Billboard.

**Conan Lee Gray** (born December 5, 1998) is an American singer, songwriter and former YouTuber. He was born in Lemon Grove, California, and raised in Georgetown, Texas, where he began uploading vlogs, covers, and original songs to YouTube as a teenager. In 2018, Gray signed a record deal with Republic Records, which released his debut EP, _Sunset Season_ (2018).
Bolstered by the commercially successful songs "Maniac" and "Heather", his studio album _Kid Krow_ (2020), entered the U.S. _Billboard_ 200 at number five, making it the biggest U.S. artist debut of that year. His second studio album, _Superache_ (2022), debuted in the top ten in the chart, also doing so in the United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland, and the Netherlands. His third and fourth albums, _Found Heaven_ (2024) and _Wishbone_ (2025), peaked at numbers 14 and three on the _Billboard_ 200, respectively.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-1)

## Early life
Gray was born on December 5, 1998, in Lemon Grove, California, a suburb of San Diego.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Notion-4) His father is Irish and his mother is Japanese.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-5) As an infant, he moved with his family to Hiroshima, Japan, because his grandfather needed medical care after being diagnosed with cancer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Mier-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Cardenas-7) After his grandfather's death, the family moved back to California.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Lauren-8)
Gray's parents divorced when he was three years old and he was thereafter raised by a single mother.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Greenwood-9) In a "Draw My Life" video, he details his experiences with divorce as a young child.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:4-10) As his father was in the military, Gray moved nine times during his childhood, including two times during sixth grade. He was frequently bullied in grade school for being quiet.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-11)
Gray eventually settled as a preteen in Georgetown, Texas, where he remained for the rest of his teenage years. His life in central Texas inspired much of his art and music. He was accepted to UCLA, and moved to Los Angeles, California, in September 2017. However, he dropped out three months later to begin touring after he was signed to Republic Records.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-12)

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
Gray created his official YouTube channel in 2013,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Metro-13) and began making videos at age 15. His early videos were about topics such as baking and mainly focused on his everyday life.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:1-14) His vlog content centered heavily on his life in small-town Texas. He is often hailed for his appreciation of Americana-related nostalgia.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Paper-15) Gray has recorded music, showed his art, and created other videos for his vlog with more than 25 million views.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Greenwood-9)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:1-14)

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
Gray self-released his debut single, "Idle Town", in March 2017. The song gained over 14 million streams on Spotify and 12 million views on YouTube.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Paper-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-ido-16) He self-released his second single, "Grow", on September 1, 2017.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-18)_[non-primary source needed_] In October 2018, he released the single "Generation Why" on Republic Records,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-ido-16) which was called "a rallying call to millennials".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-19) In November 2018, he released the five-track EP _Sunset Season_, which includes the songs "Idle Town", "Generation Why", "Crush Culture", "Greek God", and "Lookalike". The EP peaked at No. 2 on the _Billboard_ Heatseekers Albums chart. Gray embarked on the Sunset Shows tour in support of the EP.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-20) Sometime in 2018, he trademarked GirlyBoy, Inc., his way of owning his masters. He used it for his fourth album, _Wishbone_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-21)

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
Gray made his late-night television debut on _Late Night with Seth Meyers_ on the eve of February 2019,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-23) before performing several shows as an opening act on Panic! at the Disco's Pray for the Wicked Tour.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Stan-24) He played concert festivals such as The Great Escape in addition to touring nationally.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-25) In February 2019, Gray re-released the single "The Other Side"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-The_Other_Side_Affinity-26) after originally publishing it on YouTube in 2016 on the eve of the first day of his senior year of high school.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-The_Other_Side_Affinity-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-The_Other_Side_MV-27) Between March and October 2019, he released three singles from his debut album, _Kid Krow_, "Checkmate", "Comfort Crowd", and "Maniac",[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-28) and an independent single, "The King".

## Career
### 2013–2019: YouTube channel and _Sunset Season_
In October 2019, Gray embarked on the Comfort Crowd Tour, his second headlining tour of North America, with support from acclaimed New Zealand musician Benee as well as American recording artist UMI.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-29) As of October 2019, Gray's catalog had gained over 250 million streams across all platforms collectively.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-30) He received the 2019 Shorty Award for Best YouTube Musician,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-Shorty_Awards-31) and was nominated for Breakthrough Artist at the 2019 Streamy Awards.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray#cite_note-:3-32)
